read_from: The route text as served: field 1 (the route text) of each row of reader/data/route-store of the main branch at commit 306f3b285898, store_version 87b13b1169b4 (its index.json), for "OmegaWiki structured Hebrew-English DefinedMeaning relations and definitions" (M32): 5,363 routes (axis: routes), 2,605 letters keys (axis: keys). The definition field of the same row equals the route text on 5,363 of the routes. The source audit: the dictionary store's 5,697 records of this source each hold one text, in field D (2,970, the text of a defined meaning's definition) or in field R (2,727, an expression that stands on a defined meaning), and each names its defined meaning in the lane's copy of the source (the OmegaWiki lexical dump of 30 May 2023, in ledgers/work/ldmprs/source-cache/omegawiki-lexical-2026-07-14/). Joined by letters key and text, with a line break in the record taken as a space as the store takes it, 2,814 routes come from field D, 2,546 from field R, and 3 join no record; 5,357 routes stand on exactly one defined meaning and 3 on more than one (axis: routes). The audit is evidence about the source and no part of any test. The source's own key to its signs: none found. The lane holds 10 files of the source's own pages and of its mirror (the archived help page on the downloads, the mirror's dataset card and record, the licence pages, the manifests), and none holds a word that names a sign or an abbreviation; the dump's 22 tables are lexical data with no help pages: the search, its word list and the table names are builder/05-key-search.mjs and source-audit/key-search.json. The credits' short names (for example «MGH») have no key on file either. So every shape's meaning here begins "unverified:".

definitions.terms: In every test a character is one Unicode code point (every route holds only characters of 16 bits, so a code point is one index of the JavaScript string). A letter is any character of Unicode category L (JavaScript \p{L}), of any script and in either case; uppercase means Unicode category Lu. A digit is one of 0 to 9, and no test asks for any other number character. A space is the character U+0020 only, and no test uses whitespace of any other kind. Nothing is trimmed: the text is the whole route text as it stands, which is the field route of a line of the by-source JSONL, what the checker gives the classifier, and never the field def; the text before and the text after the mark are the template's c.before and c.after; what a bracket holds is the template's c.group, the same for an opener and for its closer; the innermost bracket is the template's c.container, whose values are «top», «paren» (round), «bracket» (square), «angle» and «brace». Directly before and directly after name the one character next to the mark or next to the named string; where the mark or the string stands at that end of the text no character stands there, so a test that asks for a character there fails. The whole text, exactly, means that the text equals the named string character for character. Ends in means that the last characters of the named thing are exactly the string, and starts with means that its first characters are exactly the string; neither needs a word end, and each is a run of characters and not a whole word. The word round the mark means three runs put together, with nothing between them: the run of letters that ends directly before the mark, taken back to the first character that is not a letter or to the start of the text; the mark itself; and the run of letters that begins directly after the mark, taken on to the first character that is not a letter or to the end of the text. A string stands between « and », which are not part of it, and a full stop after » belongs to the sentence and not to the string. Every string and every list minds case and is matched exact to the character. No test uses the words begins with or contains.
definitions.first_match: For each mark the shapes are tried in the order they stand in this file; the first whose test holds names the occurrence, and no later shape is tried for it. Not caught above means that no earlier shape of the same mark took the occurrence.
definitions.cut_list_match: Each string of a cut list holds its own mark once. Split the string at that one mark into a first part and a second part. An occurrence matches the string when the text before the mark ends in the first part and the text after the mark starts with the second part. An occurrence matches the list when it matches one of its strings.
definitions.whole_note: A text is a whole note when (it starts with «[» and ends in «]») or (the whole text, exactly, is one of the strings in kind_of_word_notes) or (it starts with one of the strings in kind_of_word_note_openings).
definitions.unbalanced: The ask's helper of rule 3, copied byte for byte: go through the text from its start with an empty stack; push each opener of ( [ < {; at each closer of ) ] > }, pop if the stack's top is its partner, otherwise the text does not balance; at the end the text does not balance if the stack is not empty.

The source's own dump gives each meaning a defined-meaning id and each word an expression id, and the store's record keeps them in its location field, but the route store carries neither. Each wording could stand alone in a pill. No rule can find these rows, so the ledger lists the places by hand. Should each wording print as its own reading?
